newsitem.title: UK: United Utilities sees more savings, sales cash.
newsitem.headline: United Utilities sees more savings, sales cash.

text.p: British multi-utility United Utilities Plc said Norweb, the regional electricity company which it bought last year, was providing greater savings than expected and cash proceeds from disposals should exceed targets.

The company said in a statement on Thursday that first half pretax profits rose to 223.9 million pounds ($375.9 million) from 167 million pounds previously and paid out an interim dividend of 12.0 pence, up 13.9 percent.
United Utilities said it intended to make a further initiative in the second half aimed at sharing outperformance with all its stakeholders, but gave no further details.
It said proceeds of sales of non-core businesses should exceed 400 million pounds "by a good margin," and should be completed by the end of the year.
The company said that its gearing was cut by eight percent in the first half to 81 percent at September 30 and added that its position at the full year should be similar.

United Utilities was formed when North West Water bought Norweb last year and the company said the acquisition, taking account of net debt acquired and disposals proceeds, had cost 1.335 billion or 610 pounds per customer.
